title: PDAC vs adjacent pancreas
subtitle: 24 samples · bulk RNA-seq
description: Bulk RNA-seq of 12 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDAC) and 12 paired adjacent pancreas samples from the NCI Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC-3; NCI Genomic Data Commons, data release 46.0), compared with Cellaris.
bannerText: Public bulk RNA-seq of 12 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas and 12 adjacent pancreas samples from the same patients (CPTAC-3, NCI Genomic Data Commons), compared with Cellaris. This demo shows bulk-level comparisons and estimated composition; cell-type-level comparisons are not shown for this dataset.
compareNote: Cell-type-level comparisons are not shown for this dataset: the results below compare the bulk samples. Estimated composition is shown for orientation.

pathways.themeCaveat: Themes that share hub genes (ribosomal proteins, histones, proteasome subunits) can be called from those shared genes alone. Hallmark and PROGENy sets are shown next to their best-matching sets from other databases.

composition.banner: These samples are not well described by the healthy human pancreas cell types of the built-in reference. Estimated fractions describe each sample as a mixture of healthy pancreas cell types only; cell types that the reference lacks (for example tumor cells) cannot be estimated and are absorbed into the nearest types.
composition.test: two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum per cell type; Benjamini-Hochberg across the nine types

limitations: Some samples lie outside the healthy pancreas reference (5 of 12 tumors and 2 of 12 adjacent samples flagged). Their estimated fractions describe them as mixtures of healthy pancreas cell types; tumor cells cannot be estimated and are absorbed into the nearest types.
Cell-type-level comparisons, estimated single-cell profiles and cell-level pathway activity are not shown for this dataset.
Differential expression and pathway enrichment use the bulk counts. They combine differences in composition with differences within cell types.
Each patient contributes one tumor and one adjacent sample; the comparison is adjusted for the patient.
Adjacent pancreas is tissue next to a tumor, not pancreas from healthy donors.
For research use only. Not for diagnostic use.
